text.text_excerpt: Reading recent reviews, and mine from long ago, is highly amusing due to predictability. Yes, when you don't live in nola/havent before, I wouldn't advise you to come to the Goldmine. I always ended up here at the end of the night in the quarter, as despite always being dressed in NY dresses and heels which looks absurd anywhere you go in new orleans, it was a great time at the goldmine (and honestly no dirtier or trashier than anywhere else in nola. thats what nola IS). My three friends from NYC all had a great time here the nights we went, and theyve changed up the playlist!! Had a few of the old typical Goldmine throwbacks, but new songs as well, which was a nice surprise. Ran into old...

i love this place. you can't go in expecting the best - you have to take it for what it is. cheap drinks, good music, sloppy behaviour and NOLA debauchery. if you are looking for a classy place, this is not it - this city as a whole may not be it either. come here after a few drinks and if you are looking to boogie. music is usually pretty decent - top hits kind of vibe with lots of throwbacks. this is the kind of spot that should be your last stop in your night. i promise you'll have fun! also, one of the last places that still sets your flaming dr pepper shots on fire! if you've never had one, get one. they are delicious! It's Mardi Gras weekend, and all the stories from the weekend from my friends back home in Louisiana, are filtering in. A big group of friends got done with the Endymion Ball last night, and where did they go? Not Bourbon St, but Gold Mine! I really miss this place. It's been about 3 years since i've set foot in Gold Mine. I see the tourists complaining about expensive drinks. Here's a tip folks, go to Tropical Isle, grab yourselves 4 or 5 hand grenades and drink as fast as possible. Then go to Gold Mine and take 1 or 2 Flaming Dr Pepper shots.
